claims.claim: Augustine of Hippo was a Christian bishop.
Augustine was bishop of Hippo from 396 to 430.
On the Divination of Demons was written between approximately 406 and 410.
The work was prompted by a conversation during Holy Week with lay Christian brothers who were repeating arguments from their pagan acquaintances.
The specific occasion was a question about why a pagan oracle had successfully predicted the downfall of the Serapeum, the temple of Serapis in Alexandria.
The destruction of the Temple of Serapis in Alexandria occurred in 391.
Augustine wrote the treatise to explain why and how demons achieve their apparent powers of clairvoyance.
The work reveals much about the state of pagan practice and sentiment in North Africa at the time of its composition.
The work is a combination of both a dialogue and a theological treatise.

Christian interaction with pagan religion was an object of much discussion at the end of the 4th and the beginning of the 5th century because of various imperial decrees banning pagan worship and ordering the destruction of temples.
